title: O, He Whom Jesus Loved Has Truly Spoken
description: O, He Whom Jesus Loved Has Truly Spoken in Tonic Solfa to HENLEY, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Greenleaf Whittier wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 578, “True Worship and Undefiled”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10) (11.10.11.10), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HENLEY; any other Elevens and Tens (11.10.11.10) tune fits them as well.
underlay: O, he whom Je-sus loved has tru-ly spo-ken! The holi-er wor-ship, which God deigns to bless, Re-stores the lost, and heals the spir-it bro-ken, And feeds the wid-ow and the fa-ther-less.

lines: O, he whom Jesus loved has truly spoken!
The holier worship, which God deigns to bless,
Restores the lost, and heals the spirit-broken,
And feeds the widow and the fatherless.
Then, brother man, fold to thy heart thy brother!
For where love dwells, the peace of God is there;
To worship rightly is to love each other;
Each smile a hymn, each kindly deed a prayer.
Follow, with reverent steps, the great example
Of him whose holy work was doing good:
So shall the wide earth seem our Father's temple,
Each loving life a psalm of gratitude.
Thus shall all shackles fall; the stormy clangor
Of wild war-music o'er the earth shall cease;
Love shall tread out the baleful fire of anger,
And in its ashes plant the tree of peace.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Greenleaf Whittier died in 1892.
credits: Words by John Greenleaf Whittier (1807–1892), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to HENLEY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
